html:
The Methow are an Interior Salish people of the Methow Valley in north-central Washington, which runs down from the Cascades to the Columbia River. They spoke a dialect close to that of the Okanagan.

They fished the salmon runs of the Methow and Columbia, hunted deer in the valley and gathered roots and berries, wintering in villages near the river mouth. In 1879 their land became part of the short-lived Moses or Columbia Reservation, which was opened to settlers a few years later. Most Methow moved to the Colville Reservation, where they are one of the twelve confederated bands. See also Moses-Columbia.
